title: ELF relocation types (x86-64)
summary: ELF relocations tell the linker/loader how to patch addresses. Common x86-64 relocation types: R_X86_64_NONE (0), R_X86_64_64 (1, S + A), R_X86_64_PC32 (2, S + A - P), R_X86_64_GOT32 (3), R_X86_64_PLT32 (4), R_X86_64_COPY (5), R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT (6), R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT (7), R_X86_64_RELATIVE (8, B + A), R_X86_64_32 (10), R_X86_64_32S (11), R_X86_64_16 (12), R_X86_64_PC64 (24), R_X86_64_GOTOFF64 (25), R_X86_64_GOTPC32 (26), R_X86_64_GOT64 (27).

Common x86-64 relocation types: R_X86_64_NONE (0), R_X86_64_64 (1, S + A), R_X86_64_PC32 (2, S + A - P), R_X86_64_GOT32 (3), R_X86_64_PLT32 (4), R_X86_64_COPY (5), R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT (6), R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT (7), R_X86_64_RELATIVE (8, B + A), R_X86_64_32 (10), R_X86_64_32S (11), R_X86_64_16 (12), R_X86_64_PC64 (24), R_X86_64_GOTOFF64 (25), R_X86_64_GOTPC32 (26), R_X86_64_GOT64 (27).

structure.meaning: S + A - P (PC-relative 32-bit). Used for calls/jumps.
L + A - P (PLT entry, for lazy binding).
Copy symbol data (for shared library data). Used for R_386_COPY.
B + A (base + offset, for PIE/shared libs).
G + GOT + A - P (GOT PC-relative, most common for data access).

notes: Relocations are applied by the linker (static) or dynamic loader (runtime).
GOT (Global Offset Table) enables position-independent code.
PLT (Procedure Linkage Table) enables lazy binding of shared library functions.
RELATIVE relocations are the most common in PIE/shared libraries.
